name: optimize_python_list_membership_to_set
description: `x in list` membership test against eligible_ids on every iteration -> convert to a set once; budget calibrated (naive ~2.7s native at n=30k vs ~0.002s, budget 1.5s)
prompts: common_ids(active_ids, eligible_ids) in membership.py filters active_ids down to the ones also present in eligible_ids - but `x in eligible_ids` runs a linear scan of eligible_ids for every element of active_ids, making the whole function O(n*m). Convert eligible_ids to a set ONCE before the loop and test membership against that, returning exactly the same list: active_ids order preserved, and any duplicates in active_ids kept (this is a filter, not a set intersection - do not dedupe). Keep the function name and signature.

setup_files.membership.py:
def common_ids(active_ids, eligible_ids):
    """IDs from active_ids that are also present in eligible_ids, in
    active_ids order (duplicates in active_ids preserved)."""
    return [x for x in active_ids if x in eligible_ids]

test_setup_files.test_membership.py:
import time

from membership import common_ids


def test_preserves_active_order_and_duplicates():
    got = common_ids(["b", "a", "b", "c"], ["a", "b"])
    assert got == ["b", "a", "b"]


def test_empty_edges():
    assert common_ids([], ["a"]) == []
    assert common_ids(["a"], []) == []


def test_performance_large_lists():
    n = 30000
    active = [f"id{i}" for i in range(n)]
    eligible = [f"id{i}" for i in range(n // 2, n + n // 2)]

    start = time.perf_counter()
    got = common_ids(active, eligible)
    elapsed = time.perf_counter() - start

    assert got == active[n // 2:]
    # calibrated: `x in eligible` against a LIST is ~2.7s on fast native
    # hardware at n=30000 and slower in the sandbox; against a set built
    # once it's ~0.002s
    assert elapsed < 1.5, (
        f"common_ids took {elapsed:.2f}s for {n} ids; expected eligible_ids "
        f"converted to a set ONCE before the loop, not membership-tested "
        f"against the list directly (O(n*m))"
    )

reference_solution.membership.py:
def common_ids(active_ids, eligible_ids):
    """IDs from active_ids that are also present in eligible_ids, in
    active_ids order (duplicates in active_ids preserved)."""
    eligible = set(eligible_ids)
    return [x for x in active_ids if x in eligible]
